client_alerts.headline: Meta's newest flagship model has no confirmed EU availability
client_alerts.body: Muse Spark 1.3 (Sept 2) is Meta's third proprietary release in eight weeks — closed weights, 1M context, $1.25/$4.25 per million tokens — with no confirmed EU rollout. Flag for any client using or evaluating Meta AI models where EU data residency or GDPR alignment matters.

top_moves.title: OpenAI ships a misalignment transparency framework
top_moves.body: A new framework for tracking and disclosing model misalignment, plus six reports on unexpected or concerning model behavior, aims to speed public transparency on frontier model risk.

top_moves.title: Claude Code beta: one project now coordinates parallel work
top_moves.body: A new beta lets a single Claude Code project run parallel threads, shared memory, and a project library to manage long-running work — plus auto mode now defaults to server-side classifier billing so API/Enterprise users aren't charged for classifier overhead.

top_moves.title: Meta quietly pivots to closed-weight models outside the Llama brand
top_moves.body: Muse Spark 1.3 is Meta's third proprietary flagship release in eight weeks — closed weights, no confirmed EU availability — a notable break from the open-weight Llama strategy clients may be architecting around.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: New misalignment tracking/disclosure framework ships alongside six model-behavior transparency reports; GPT-6 Astra rollout continues.
providers.detail: OpenAI released a framework for tracking and disclosing model misalignment plus six reports on unexpected model behavior, aiming to speed transparency and alignment research. GPT-6 Astra's stable release (Sept 14) continues rolling into Work, Codex and API. ChatGPT Images 2.5 added a Sketch-to-image feature with 50% lower generation latency.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Claude Code beta adds parallel-thread project coordination; auto mode drops classifier-overhead charges for API/Enterprise.
providers.detail: A new beta Claude Code projects experience lets one project coordinate parallel threads, shared memory and a project library for long-running work. Auto mode now defaults to server-side classifier billing, which doesn't charge for classifier overhead. Anthropic also shipped 43 new Small Business workflows and 27 connectors (Shopify, Salesforce, Zoom, Xero, Gusto, Square, Stripe, Zapier), and cancelled the scheduled Sonnet 5 price increase — it stays at $2/$10 per million tokens.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Gemini Live 3.8 and Live Extended Thinking reach general availability alongside a new Transcribe model.
providers.detail: Gemini 3.8 Live and Live Extended Thinking (audio-to-audio, real-time voice) are now GA. Gemini Omni Flash is GA with video-extension continuations and a resolution parameter up to 4K. Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, a new speech-to-text model, targets voice agents and live captioning. Gemini 3.7 Flash continues rolling out for coding and long-horizon agent work.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Grok 4.7's rollout continues expanding into enterprise and dev tools after finally shipping Monday.
providers.detail: Grok 4.7 (2.1T parameters, up 40% from Grok 4.6; $2/$6 per million tokens) shipped Sept 21 after missing its Sept 12 target twice, with improved self-verification and long-context management. It's live day-one in GitHub Copilot and Cursor. Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 also shipped this month with stronger multilingual accuracy, diarization and turn detection.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: Muse Spark 1.3 — Meta's third proprietary release in eight weeks — ships closed-weight with no confirmed EU availability.
providers.detail: Muse Spark 1.3 rolled out in Muse Code and the Meta Model API (also via OpenRouter) with 1M context at $1.25/$4.25 per million tokens. Unlike Llama, it's closed-weight with no EU availability confirmed — a signal Meta may be de-emphasizing open weights for its newest flagship work.
providers.alertReason: No confirmed EU availability — data residency/GDPR implications for clients evaluating Meta models.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: Quiet week — OCR 4.1 GA and Agentic Search stand; Leanstral 1.5 retires Sept 30.
providers.detail: No new headline release today. Mistral OCR 4.1 remains GA, and the new Agentic Search retrieval layer (via Search Toolkit and Libraries) continues rolling out for document navigation and verification. Leanstral 1.5, the Lean 4 formal-proof model, is scheduled to retire Sept 30, 2026.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: Agent API adds custom MCP connectors; remote MCP server now supports OAuth sign-in.
providers.detail: Perplexity's Agent API now supports custom connectors so users can bring their own MCP servers (credentials stored by Perplexity, API-key or no-auth over Streamable HTTP/SSE). The remote Perplexity MCP Server added OAuth sign-in, replacing pasted API keys in clients like Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code. Computer also added Light-to-Ultra effort controls for model selection, and HP is now preloading the Perplexity Windows app.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Teams Facilitator can auto-post a Copilot web search answer into meeting chat; Cowork adds a GPT/Claude model picker.
providers.detail: Facilitator (Copilot Premium) can run a web search and post the answer into meeting chat when a factual question goes unanswered, capped to roughly once per meeting. Meeting recaps can now be translated into a chosen language. Cowork's model picker (GPT vs. Claude sections) is now built into the prompt box with a reasoning-effort slider, and individual responses or chat sessions can now be shared via link.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: CLI v1.0.87 adds prompt-recall shortcuts; selected Copilot models face an Oct 19 deprecation cutoff.
providers.detail: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.87 (Sept 21) adds keyboard shortcuts to recall and edit pending messages; v1.0.86 (Sept 17) makes custom instructions persist across sessions; v1.0.85 (Sept 16) adds Vim mode. Separately, GitHub announced deprecation of selected Copilot models across chat, inline edits, agent modes and completions, effective Oct 19, 2026.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new release today; Claude Fable 5.1 integration and self-hosted machines remain the latest ships.
providers.detail: No material update surfaced today. Cursor's most recent ships remain Claude Fable 5.1 model integration and self-hosted machine support.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No headline release today — over 90 days quiet since June 12.
providers.detail: Gamma remains quiet with no new feature releases surfacing in search this run.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new headline today; Notion 3.7's Agent Skills library and per-agent model controls remain the latest ships.
providers.detail: No new material surfaced today beyond what's already tracked: Notion 3.7 (Sept 15) added a shared Agent Skills library for teams, and the Sept 9 release let workspace owners set per-agent default AI models on Business/Enterprise plans. AI Search is now reported 50% faster.

xAI — Grok 4.7 saga — 3 weeks running (missed its Sept 12 target twice, finally shipped Sept 21, now expanding into enterprise tools)
Mistral — OCR 4.1 GA / Agentic Search — 3 weeks running quiet (Leanstral 1.5 retires Sept 30)
Google Gemini — Live/Omni voice & video expansion — 2 weeks running (Daily Brief and hands-free inbox last week, now Live 3.8 and Transcribe GA)

month_themes.then: No month-ago snapshot yet — history tracking began within the last month.
month_themes.now: Frontier model iteration accelerating (GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.7, Gemini 3.8); agentic workflow coordination maturing (Claude Code projects, Notion Agent Skills, Perplexity MCP connectors); governance and disclosure pressure building (OpenAI's misalignment framework, NIST's AI documentation draft, Meta's closed-weight pivot).

habits.shift: Sonnet 5's price increase was cancelled — it holds at $2/$10/M tokens. Keep it as the default drafting model; the new Claude Code beta's parallel-thread project coordination is worth piloting for multi-runbook engagements.
NIST's public-facing AI documentation 'Zero Draft' comment window closed Sept 16 — guidance is still in flux, so treat any AI-generated standards summary as provisional until the revision lands.
Flag Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 pivot to closed weights and no EU availability for any client whose architecture assumes open Llama weights.
ChatGPT's native Microsoft Word integration is now stable enough to draft, revise and format SOWs directly in the sidebar rather than round-tripping through copy/paste.
No material change this week — keep current tooling.
Two new GA speech-to-text models this month (diarization, multichannel, word timestamps) are worth a pilot for automating meeting-note capture on client calls.
